claim_summary: The paper contributes an appliance-energy pipeline combining forecasting and calibrated anomaly detection with context-conditioned LLM diagnoses, safety rules, operator-feedback memory, and prioritized maintenance recommendations.

claim_evidence.quote: We presented Smart Energy Agent, a hybrid pipeline combining deep forecasting, anomaly detection, retrievalaugmented LLM reasoning, and operator feedback for appliance-level energy management.

modules.name: SSA-LSTM appliance forecasting backbone
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because the module produces an appliance forecast for a defined horizon; changing task family requires changing the prediction objective and output. Its lagged temporal inputs do not make it task-general GTS infrastructure, so R3_2 does not apply.
rubric_path: R1:contributed - custom global SSA-LSTM forecasting model
R2:Harness - a forecasting capability executed around the LLM

evidence.quote: The forecasting backbone is a single global model with separate LSTM branches for each SSA component (trend, seasonality, residual) and an additional branch for exogenous features. A learned per-appliance embedding allows specialization without per-device training.

Inputs include lagged consumption values, rolling statistics, and cyclic time encodings. The model is trained once on a chronological 70/15/15 split and deployed in inferenceonly mode every 30 minutes.

modules.name: Per-appliance LSTM-VAE detector and calibrated thresholds
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because reconstruction scores and appliance-specific thresholds directly define anomaly flags; another task family requires a different detector objective and decision threshold. Sliding windows and chronological calibration are temporal, but this is task-bound anomaly logic rather than general GTS infrastructure, so R3_2 does not apply.
rubric_path: R1:contributed - per-appliance LSTM-VAE models and threshold calibration
R2:Harness - detector tools supplying evidence to the LLM workflow

evidence.quote: Anomaly Detector: Seven independent LSTM-VAE models with multi-head attention and percentilebased thresholds.
The detection threshold τ is the p-th percentile of validation scores (chronological middle 15%, used solely for calibration),
with p tuned per appliance: Microwave 97.0%, Printer 98.5%, Fridge/Kettle/Coffee Machine 99.0%, Water Dispenser 99.5%, and Tasmota 99.9%.

modules.name: Event-conditioned two-tier context retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because source selection is conditioned on appliance-event ambiguity, severity, and baseline sparsity to support anomaly diagnosis and recommendations; changing task family requires redesigning its evidence sources and selection criteria. Although it uses temporal history and time-of-day context, it is task-bound rather than a general temporal service, so R3_2 does not apply.
rubric_path: R2:Harness - prompt-time retrieval tools without model parameter updates
R4:Memory and Context; Tools and Execution; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: The first three are retrieved unconditionally — the agent must always know detector reliability, the time-of-day baseline, and domain knowledge before reasoning.
The remaining three are conditionally selected based on signal ambiguity, event severity, or baseline sparsity, keeping the diagnosis prompt focused and free of irrelevant context.

modules.name: Reliability-aware appliance diagnosis and reporting
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because the event coordinator, diagnostic routing, reliability caps, and urgency rules embed appliance-anomaly diagnosis criteria; changing task family requires redesigning the event states and verifiers. It uses temporal history and time-of-day rules but is task-bound, so it does not meet R3_2's general temporal-service condition.
rubric_path: R1:contributed - hybrid rule/LLM diagnosis, safety nets, event coordination, and prioritized reporting
R2:Harness - runtime workflow around an unchanged LLM
R3_1_TSK:yes - anomaly diagnosis and recommendation criteria
R4:Tools and Execution; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: Coordinator: Groups events by time and appliance, filters borderline cases, and caps LLM calls per run.
The Diagnosis Agent routes each event through hybrid rule + LLM logic across three paths: Path 1 returns a deterministic “inspect now” diagnosis for devices completely inactive for several days

urgency fallback, a confidence fallback, a reliability cap that lowers confidence for known noisy detectors, and a night-time hard rule that forces immediate urgency for fridge or water dispenser anomalies between 10 PM and 6 AM.
The Report Agent converts the structured JSON into a prioritized Markdown report grouped by urgency.

modules.name: Operator-feedback memory for future diagnoses
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because operator corrections are matched by appliance and anomaly pattern to revise future anomaly diagnoses; changing task family requires redesigning the match keys and correction semantics. The time-of-day window is temporal, but the memory is tied to this diagnosis task rather than a general temporal service, so R3_2 does not apply.
rubric_path: R1:contributed - persistent operator corrections injected into future prompts
R2:Harness - memory augments prompts without changing LLM parameters
R3_1_TSK:yes - feedback memory is specific to anomaly diagnosis
R4:Memory and Context; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: Operator corrections are appended to feedback_log.csv via the dashboard feedback form.

corrections matching the current event by appliance, pattern type, and time-of-day window are injected into the diagnosis prompt, providing a reflective memory that progressively reduces repeated false alarms.

temporal_validity.quote: All experiments are conducted on a chronological train/validation/test split of the appliance-level dataset. The validation set (the middle 15%) is used solely for threshold calibration; metrics are reported on the held-out test set.

task_performance.quote: The model achieves an R2 of 0.9976 and a Weighted Absolute Percentage Error (WAPE) of 1.32%, indicating that variance is well captured at the aggregate level.

changes: Split event-conditioned context retrieval from diagnosis/reporting while retaining the existing id for the diagnosis/reporting mechanism.
dimensions: removed Memory and Context from the diagnosis module; replaced retired Planning and Workflow with Planning and Orchestration.
reconciliation.reason: The packet describes a distinct Context Agent that selects evidence before the Diagnosis Agent routes events and the Report Agent renders recommendations. These mechanisms are separable, so retrieval receives a new module id and the existing id remains on diagnosis/reporting. The separately described feedback memory and the forecasting and anomaly-detection models are also added as source-supported modules.

notes: The operator-feedback memory is implemented, but its impact on accuracy is explicitly left unquantified (lines 493-498). The paper reports task-output performance, not downstream cost, profit, or utility of maintenance decisions.
